newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss M0 grew 6.3 pct in Q2 vs Q4.
newsitem.headline: Swiss M0 grew 6.3 pct in Q2 vs Q4.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) said that its key monetary aggregate, the M0, was growing at an annualised rate of 6.3 percent in the second quarter of 1997 (not in June-July) versus the fourth quarter of 1996.
The data were contained in the preliminary release of the SNB's monthly report for mid-June to mid-July.
In the second quarter, the seasonally-adjusted M0 averaged 32.758 billion Swiss francs.
In the month of June alone, M0 grew at an annualised rate of 6.0 percent versus fourth quarter 1996.

The SNB said sight deposits averaged 3.991 billion Swiss francs in June, which was 262 million higher than in May. Notes in circulation rose by 2.35 percent versus June 1996 to 28.71 billion Swiss francs.
The overall M0 aggregate, which comprises sight deposits and notes in circulation, rose by 14 million Swiss francs to 32.865 billion francs in June versus May.
